units.title: This, That, These, Those
notes: This (one) and These (two or more) are near you: This is my pen.
That (one) and Those (two or more) are far away: Those are chairs.
This and That take is. These and Those take are.

items.why: One thing and is, so This.
Two or more and are, so Those.
After These we say are.
After That we say is.

items.q: Come here! ___ is my new sharpener.
items.why: One thing near you, so This.

items.q: Look over there! ___ are my friends.
items.why: Two or more far away, so Those.
This is a + one thing, no -s.
Those are + two or more, with -s.
One thing, so It's.
Two or more things, so They're.
One chair, so This chair.
Two or more notebooks, so Those.

items.q: Is that your tape? Yes, ___ is.
items.why: One thing, so Yes, it is.

items.q: Are these your markers? Yes, ___ are.
items.why: Two or more things, so Yes, they are.
After Those we say are.
After This we say is.

items.q: That is one desk. Those are two ___ (desk).
items.why: Two things, so add -s.
Markers is plural, so this changes to these.

items.q: a / that / pencil case / is / yellow
a: That is a yellow pencil case.
Is that a yellow pencil case?
items.why: That is a + one thing.
Scissors is plural, so Those are.

units.title: To be; have got
notes: I am, you are, he / she / it is, we / they are: She is happy.
Negative: I'm not, he isn't, they aren't.
I / you / we / they have got. He / she / it has got: He has got two eyes.
Negative: haven't got, hasn't got. Question: Has she got long hair?

items.why: After I we say am.
My friends are they, so are.
He is happy, so he isn't angry.
With you we say Are.
Yes, she is.
No, they aren't.
In English we use be for age.
After I we say have got.
One alien is it, so has got.
After She we say has got.
A snake is it, so hasn't got.
With he we say Has he got...?

items.q: Have you got a sister? Yes, I ___.
items.why: Yes, I have.
With I we say haven't got.
My brother is he, so is.
After He we say has got.

items.q: They ___ (not be) sad. They are happy.
items.why: After They we say aren't.
After I we say haven't got.

items.q: got / my / eyes / has / friend / brown
a: My friend has got brown eyes.
Has my friend got brown eyes?
items.why: The colour goes before the noun.

units.title: Present simple
notes: I / you / we / they play. He / she / it plays, with -s.
Special forms: he goes, she watches, he does, she has.
Negative: I don't play. He doesn't play.
Do you play tennis? Yes, I do. / No, I don't.

items.why: My sister is she, so add -s.
After We the verb has no -s.
Watch takes -es with he.

items.q: I ___ go to school on Sundays.
items.why: With I the negative is don't.
With she the negative is doesn't.
After doesn't the verb has no -s.

items.q: ___ you play tennis? Yes, I do.
items.why: With you the question starts with Do.

items.q: Do you wake up early? No, I ___.
items.why: No, I don't.
With she the question starts with Does.
Have changes to has with he.
After I the verb does not change.

items.q: She ___ to bed late on Saturdays.
items.why: Go takes -es with she.

items.q: I ___ wake up late on Mondays.
items.why: Never goes before the verb.

items.q: Does he play football? Yes, he ___.
items.why: Yes, he does.

items.q: He ___ (go) to bed late every day.
items.why: Go takes -es with he.
After we the verb has no -s.
With she we say doesn't + verb.
Have changes to has with she.

items.q: breakfast / I / at / have / always / home
a: I always have breakfast at home.
At home I always have breakfast.
items.why: Always goes before the verb.

items.q: you / on / what / do / Saturdays / do
a: What do you do on Saturdays?
items.why: What + do + you + verb.

units.title: Can / can't
notes: can + verb, with no -s and no to: A frog can jump.
The negative is can't: Penguins can't fly.
Can you swim? Yes, I can. / No, I can't.

items.q: A snake ___ run. It has no legs.
items.why: No legs, so it can't run.

items.q: Eagles have got wings. They ___ fly.
items.why: They have wings, so they can fly.
After can the verb has no -s and no to.
Can never changes. No -s, no to.
The answer has can, so ask with Can.

items.q: Can a kangaroo hop? Yes, it ___.
items.why: Yes, it can.
No, they can't.
In questions can goes first.

items.q: Pandas can climb, but they ___ fly.
items.why: But shows the opposite, so can't.

items.q: I can't ___. I'm scared of water.
items.why: After can't the verb does not change.
Can never takes -s.

items.q: What can you do? I ___ run and jump.
items.why: Answer with can + verb.

items.q: Can she speak English? ___, she can.
items.why: She can goes with Yes.
After can the verb does not change.
The negative of can is can't.
After can the verb has no -s.
Yes, they can.

items.q: Can your parrot sing? No, it ___ (not can).
items.why: No, it can't.

items.q: swim / a / and / can / frog / jump
a: A frog can swim and jump.
A frog can jump and swim.
Can a frog swim and jump?
Can a frog jump and swim?
items.why: can + verb.
can't + verb.

units.title: I like / She likes
notes: I / you / we / they like rice. He / she likes rice.
Negative: I don't like soup. She doesn't like soup.
After doesn't the verb has no -s: He doesn't like eggs.
Do you like bacon? Yes, I do. Does he like bacon? Yes, he does.

items.why: My brother is he, so likes.
My friends are they, so like.
With we the negative is don't.
With she the negative is doesn't.
After doesn't the verb has no -s.

items.q: ___ you like rice? Yes, I do.
items.why: With you the question starts with Do.
Your sister is she, so Does.

items.q: Do they like soup? No, they ___.
items.why: No, they don't.

items.q: Does he like lettuce? Yes, he ___.
items.why: Yes, he does.
Mum and I are we, so like.
With she the question uses does.

items.q: I like rice, but my dad ___.
items.why: My dad is he, so doesn't.
After does the verb has no -s.

items.q: He ___ soup. He eats it every day.
items.why: He eats it every day, so he likes it.

items.q: My sister ___ (like) cookies. She eats them every day.
items.why: My sister is she, so likes.

items.q: He ___ (not like) bacon. He never eats it.
items.why: With he we say doesn't like.

items.q: We ___ (not like) cold soup. We never eat it.
items.why: With we we say don't like.

items.q: Does he like eggs? No, he ___ (not do).
items.why: No, he doesn't.
doesn't + like, no -s.

items.q: you / for / what / like / breakfast / do
a: What do you like for breakfast?
items.why: What + do + you + like.

units.title: There is / There are; Where is...?
notes: There is + one thing: There is a kite in the garden.
There are + two or more things: There are two boats.
Where is the ball? It is under the bed.
Where are the marbles? They are in the box.

items.q: There ___ a puzzle on the table.
items.why: One puzzle, so There is.

items.q: There ___ ten marbles in the bag.
items.why: Ten marbles, so There are.
One skateboard, so There is.
Two helicopters, so There are.

items.q: There is ___ in the living room.
items.why: There is + one thing.
There are + two or more things.

items.q: ___ is my kite? It's in the garden.
items.why: The answer is a place, so Where.
Marbles is plural, so Where are.

items.q: Where is the bicycle? ___ in the garden.
items.why: One bicycle, so It is.

items.q: Where are my video games? ___ on the bed.
items.why: Two or more things, so They are.
Between means in the middle of two things.

items.q: There is a bath ___ the bathroom.
items.why: Things are in a room.

items.q: Is there a kite in the box? Yes, there ___.
items.why: Yes, there is.
How many + plural takes are there.
One boat, so There is.
Four kites, so There are.

items.q: Where ___ (be) my skateboard? It is here.
items.why: One skateboard, so Where is.

items.q: Where are the marbles? They ___ (be) under the sofa.
items.why: After They we say are.

items.q: a / under / there / the bed / is / puzzle
a: There is a puzzle under the bed.
Is there a puzzle under the bed?
items.why: There is + a + thing + place.
Where + are + plural.

units.title: Present continuous
notes: Use am, is or are + verb-ing for now: She is reading.
Negative: I'm not singing. He isn't dancing. They aren't skating.
Questions: What are you doing? Is he painting? Yes, he is.
Spelling: dance, dancing; ride, riding; hit, hitting.

items.q: My friends and I ___ playing hockey.
items.why: My friends and I are we, so are.
One pirate is he, so is.
After is we use the -ing form.
With you we say are.
After is we use the -ing form.
He is dancing, so he isn't singing.

items.q: Are they playing baseball? Yes, they ___.
items.why: Yes, they are.
No, she isn't.
Ride loses the e before -ing.

items.q: Look! The knight is ___ a ball.
items.why: After is we use the -ing form.
With he and -ing we ask with Is.
After I we say am.
We need is + verb-ing.
Hit has double t before -ing.
Dance loses the e before -ing.
Listen! means now, so is + singing.

items.q: I ___ (not draw) now. I am reading.
items.why: With I we say am not + verb-ing.
Now, so are + playing.

items.q: flying / my / a / is / kite / friend
a: My friend is flying a kite.
Is my friend flying a kite?
items.why: is + verb-ing.
What + are + people + doing.

units.title: Was / were
notes: Past of be: I / he / she / it was. You / we / they were.
Negative: wasn't, weren't. I wasn't at home.
Use was and were with yesterday and last Monday. Use is and are with today.

items.q: I ___ at the zoo last Saturday.
items.why: Last Saturday is past. After I we say was.

items.q: My friends ___ at the theatre yesterday.
items.why: Yesterday is past. My friends are they, so were.
Yesterday is past and it is one day, so was.
Today is the present, so are.
Yesterday is past. After It we say was.

items.q: Yesterday she ___ at school. She was sick.
items.why: Past and she, so wasn't.

items.q: Last Sunday we ___ at the park. It was raining.
items.why: Past and we, so weren't.
Yesterday is past. With you we say were.

items.q: Were you at the park? Yes, I ___.
items.why: Yes, I was.

items.q: Was he at the shop? No, he ___.
items.why: No, he wasn't.

items.q: ___ they at the amusement park yesterday?
items.why: Yesterday is past. With they we say Were.
Today is the present, so is.
Was is past, so yesterday.
Last Thursday is past. After we we say were.
Yesterday is past. After He we say was.
Last Monday is past. After We we say were.

items.q: Yesterday I ___ (not be) at school. I was sick.
items.why: Past and I, so wasn't.
Today is the present, so is.

items.q: at / my / yesterday / were / the park / friends
a: My friends were at the park yesterday.
Yesterday my friends were at the park.
Were my friends at the park yesterday?
items.why: My friends are they, so were.
After it we say wasn't.

units.title: There was / There were
notes: There was + one thing in the past: There was a cap on the chair.
There were + two or more things: There were two dresses.
Now: there is, there are. Yesterday: there was, there were.
A pair is one thing: There was a pair of trainers.

items.why: Yesterday and one cap, so was.
Last Monday and forty caps, so were.

items.q: In the old shop ___ fifty hats.
items.why: Fifty hats, so there were.

items.q: ___ a uniform on the chair yesterday.
items.why: One uniform in the past, so There was.
Now is the present, so there are.
Today is the present, so there is.
There was + one thing.

items.q: There were ___ in the beach bag.
items.why: There were + two or more things.

items.q: There ___ a pair of trainers yesterday.
items.why: A pair is one thing, so was.

items.q: There ___ two pairs of glasses yesterday.
items.why: Two pairs, so were.
Yesterday and one hat, so Was there.

items.q: Were there many dresses? Yes, there ___.
items.why: Yes, there were.

items.q: Was there a uniform? No, there ___.
items.why: No, there wasn't.

items.q: How many caps ___ there last summer?
items.why: Last summer and plural caps, so were.
Yesterday and one dress, so was.
Last summer and many caps, so were.
Now and three skirts, so are.

items.q: There ___ (not be) a cap here yesterday.
items.why: Yesterday and one cap, so wasn't.

items.q: a / in / there / swimsuit / was / the bag
a: There was a swimsuit in the bag.
Was there a swimsuit in the bag?
items.why: There was + a + thing + place.

items.q: many / in / were / the shop / there / trainers
a: There were many trainers in the shop.
Were there many trainers in the shop?
items.why: There were + plural.
